messages:
maya: Quick Q — working through a customer security questionnaire (SOC2). They asked: do we ever persist plaintext customer prompts in hosted API logs? Also want the list of encryption subprocessors (KMS, monitoring, logging) and a short description of who can access logs. Need a concise answer for the form by EOD.

irene: Short answer for the form: we do NOT persist full plaintext prompts in long-term logs. We retain request metadata and truncated prompt fingerprints for debugging and correlation. For live debug sessions there may be ephemeral snippets but those are short-lived and redacted. See internal logging policy: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/logging-redaction (internal only).

sam: Adding context: our redaction pipeline runs on ingestion and applies multiple rules. For hosted API:
```
redact_pipeline:
  - detect_pii: true
  - mask_credit_card: true
  - mask_ssn: true
  - truncate_prompt_chars: 240
```
We also keep a minimal encrypted blob for replay in case of customer debug requests (requires approvals).

compliance: For subprocessors list to include in the questionnaire: AWS KMS (key management, region: us-west-2), Datadog (metrics/log forwarding), Sentry (error telemetry), and Fastly (edge CDN). I'll assemble the official CSV export for the customer binder.

ops: Note: for Dedicated/Private customers we support customer-managed keys (BYOK). When BYOK is used, Redwood does not have access to key material and cannot decrypt customer ciphertext. For hosted KMS usage, we use AWS KMS CMKs in our account (we can provide ARNs on request).

maya: Great — can someone give me a one-line for "who can access logs" that I can paste into the questionnaire (they specifically asked for roles + approval flow)?

irene: One-liner you can paste: "Log access is restricted to SRE and Security engineers on a need-to-know basis; requests are tracked via the access portal and require manager + security approval and an audit entry." If they want more detail, say: requests use the Access Portal -> approvals by manager + security -> short-lived credentials issued -> audited in our SIEM.

sec-bot: audit: Access request record created by maya at 2012345680 for customer-sq evidence gathering. Entry id: audit-7f8b2c.

compliance: I'll draft the formal answers and DM you the evidence links (SOC2 report excerpts, logging-redaction runbook, subprocessors CSV). If they ask for timeline for SOC2 certs: we have Type II reports through 2024, next audit window in Q3 2025.

maya: Awesome, thanks all — I'll update the questionnaire and follow up if they ask for ARNs or sample logs (we should only share redacted extracts). :thumbsup:

sam: If you need a sanitized example log snippet for the binder, say so and I can produce one (no PII, masked values).

maya: Will do. Tagging @compliance when I send the draft back for sign-off.

(ends)
